problem: NLP is still dominated by text-only work, although human language use is tied to perception, action and the brain; prior VLN and grounding resources lack multilingual, spoken and fine-grained word-to-pixel aligned data.
motivation: Language understanding should be studied together with other modalities and environments, including speech. The talk argues this is now feasible and useful for both engineering and the science of language grounding.
key_idea: Language, vision and action should be modeled jointly. The talk illustrates this with speech-image retrieval, text-to-image generation, and the multilingual Room-across-Room (RxR) VLN dataset.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so the paper's analysis cannot be assessed. The abstract claims that directly encoding speech can beat the ASR + strong text encoder pipeline in some speech-image retrieval settings. It also presents RxR's spoken instructions and fine-grained word-pixel alignments as a richer grounding signal.
method: Speech-image representation learning: encodes speech directly for retrieval and compares against ASR plus text encoders.
Multi-stage text-to-image generation: uses user guidance in the form of mouse traces.
Single-stage text-to-image generation: trained with cross-modal contrastive losses.
Room-across-Room (RxR): a multilingual VLN dataset with spoken instructions, high-quality text transcriptions, and word-to-pixel alignments in HD 360-degree panoramas.
